clauses.title: Security Deposit
clauses.summary: $5,000 is double the monthly rent. Most jurisdictions cap security deposits at 1-2 months' rent. This deposit has no interest accrual and no defined return timeline -- the landlord could withhold it indefinitely.
clauses.recommendation: Negotiate the deposit down to one month's rent ($2,500) and require it be held in a separate interest-bearing account with a 30-day return deadline.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Tenant shall pay a security deposit equal to one month's rent ($2,500), to be held in a separate interest-bearing account. Landlord shall return the deposit within 30 days of lease termination, minus any itemised deductions for damages beyond normal wear and tear.
clauses.details: "Tenant shall pay a security deposit of $5,000 to be held by Landlord for the duration of the lease."

clauses.title: Late Payment Penalty
clauses.summary: $250 late fee on $2,500 rent = 10% penalty. Many jurisdictions cap late fees at 5% or less. A 3-day grace period is extremely short -- one weekend delay and you're penalized.
clauses.recommendation: Push for a 10-day grace period and cap the late fee at $50 or 5% of rent, whichever is less.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: If rent is not received by the 10th of each month, a late fee of $50 or 5% of the monthly rent (whichever is less) will be charged. Tenant shall receive a written notice before any late fee is applied.
clauses.details: "If rent is not received by the 3rd of each month, a late fee of $250 will be charged immediately."

clauses.title: Maintenance Responsibilities
clauses.summary: This clause dumps ALL repair costs on the tenant -- plumbing, electrical, HVAC. In most jurisdictions, landlords are legally required to maintain structural elements and essential systems. This is likely unenforceable.
clauses.recommendation: Split responsibilities: landlord handles structural + major systems (plumbing, electrical, HVAC), you handle minor upkeep and damage you cause.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Landlord shall be responsible for all structural repairs and maintenance of plumbing, electrical, and HVAC systems. Tenant shall be responsible for minor upkeep and any damage caused by tenant negligence.
clauses.details: "Tenant shall be responsible for all repairs and maintenance of the premises, including plumbing, electrical, and HVAC systems."

clauses.title: Early Termination
clauses.summary: You cannot leave early under ANY circumstances, and if you do, you owe ALL remaining rent immediately. No mitigation, no buyout option. Many courts won't enforce this because landlords have a duty to mitigate damages.
clauses.recommendation: Propose a buyout option: 60 days' notice + 2 months' rent as a termination fee, and the landlord must try to re-rent.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Tenant may terminate this lease early with 60 days' written notice and payment of a termination fee equal to two months' rent. Landlord shall make reasonable efforts to re-let the premises to offset remaining rent obligations.
clauses.details: "Tenant may not terminate this lease early under any circumstances. All remaining rent becomes immediately due upon vacating."

clauses.title: Entry Rights
clauses.summary: The landlord can walk in at any time, for any reason, with zero notice. This violates tenant privacy rights in virtually every jurisdiction. Standard is 24-48 hours' written notice for non-emergencies.
clauses.recommendation: Require at least 24 hours' written notice for all non-emergency entry. Entries only during reasonable hours (9am-6pm) and only for legitimate purposes.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Landlord shall provide at least 24 hours' written notice before entering the premises, except in cases of genuine emergency. Entry shall occur during reasonable hours (9am-6pm) and only for legitimate purposes (inspections, repairs, showings).
clauses.details: "Landlord may enter the premises at any time without notice for any reason."

clauses.title: Rent Increase
clauses.summary: The landlord can raise your rent by any amount with just 15 days' notice. In a 12-month lease, your rent should be fixed for the full term. This clause destroys any rent stability.
clauses.recommendation: Lock the rent for the entire lease term. If increases on renewal are allowed, require 90 days' notice and cap at CPI or 3%.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Rent shall remain fixed for the duration of the lease term. Any rent increase upon renewal shall require 90 days' written notice and shall not exceed the greater of 3% or the local CPI increase.
clauses.details: "Landlord reserves the right to increase rent at any time with 15 days' notice."

clauses.title: Liability and Insurance
clauses.summary: You take ALL liability for any injury on the property, even if it's caused by the building's condition. The landlord gets a blanket waiver. Courts typically won't enforce this -- landlords can't contract away negligence for conditions they control.
clauses.recommendation: Change to shared liability: each party is responsible for their own negligence. Require the landlord to carry property insurance.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Each party shall be responsible for liabilities arising from their own negligence. Landlord shall maintain property insurance. Tenant is encouraged to obtain renter's insurance for personal property.
clauses.details: "Tenant assumes all liability for injuries occurring on the premises, regardless of cause. Landlord shall not be held liable for any damages."

clauses.title: Lease Duration
clauses.summary: Standard 12-month fixed term. This is normal and fair.
clauses.details: "This lease shall be for a term of 12 months beginning on the move-in date specified above."

clauses.title: Monthly Rent
clauses.summary: Rent of $2,500 due on the 1st of each month. Amount and due date are clearly stated -- standard practice.
clauses.details: "Tenant agrees to pay monthly rent of $2,500, due on the 1st of each month."

clauses.title: Utilities
clauses.summary: You pay ALL utilities. While tenants often pay their own, this clause is vague about which utilities exist and doesn't clarify who pays for shared building utilities (water, trash in multi-unit buildings).
clauses.recommendation: Clarify the split: you pay electricity/gas/internet, landlord pays water/sewer/trash.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Tenant shall be responsible for electricity, gas, and internet. Landlord shall be responsible for water, sewer, and trash collection. Tenant shall set up utility accounts in their name within 5 days of move-in.
clauses.details: "Tenant shall be responsible for all utility payments including electricity, gas, water, and internet."

clauses.title: Pets Policy
clauses.summary: No pets allowed without landlord approval, but no criteria for approval are stated. The landlord could say no for any reason. Also, emotional support animals may need accommodation under fair housing laws.
clauses.recommendation: Ask for defined pet criteria and a reasonableness clause so approval can't be arbitrarily denied. Request accommodation for service/emotional support animals.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Tenant may keep up to 2 domestic pets with prior written approval (not to be unreasonably withheld). A pet deposit of $300 shall be required. Reasonable accommodations for service and emotional support animals as required by law.
clauses.details: "No pets of any kind are permitted on the premises without prior written approval from Landlord."

clauses.title: Subletting
clauses.summary: You can't sublet without landlord consent, but there's no standard for that consent. The landlord could refuse for any reason, leaving you stuck with the lease even if you need to relocate.
clauses.recommendation: Add 'shall not be unreasonably withheld' language so the landlord can't block you arbitrarily.
clauses.suggestedRewrite: Tenant may not sublet or assign the lease without prior written consent of the Landlord, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
clauses.details: "Tenant may not sublet or assign the lease without prior written consent of the Landlord."

clauses.title: Quiet Enjoyment
clauses.summary: Standard protection for your right to use the property peacefully. This is fair as written.

clauses.title: Parking
clauses.summary: One designated parking space at no extra charge. Clear and fair.

gapAnalysis.suggestion: No process exists to document the apartment's condition when you move in. Without this, the landlord could claim pre-existing damage and keep your deposit. Add a joint move-in/move-out inspection with photos.
If you and the landlord disagree about something, there's no process to resolve it. You'd go straight to court. Add a mediation clause requiring good-faith negotiation before either party can sue.
The lease doesn't mention renter's insurance. If there's a fire or flood, your personal belongings aren't covered. Add a clause requiring renter's insurance to protect your stuff.
